Product change: private projects become actually private.

Projects have a `visibility` of `private`, `org` or `public`, and explicit project membership is already stored, but today a `private` project is visible to the whole organization like any other. Enforce it.

A `private` project, and everything in it, is visible to an actor only if at least one of these holds: the actor's role is `admin` or `owner`; the actor is platform staff; the actor is the project's lead; the actor has been added to the project as a project member. `org` and `public` projects are unaffected.

To everyone else a private project must behave as if it did not exist:
- Looking up the project, one of its issues, its board, or an issue's comment thread throws `NotFoundError` (exported from `src/server/services/_support.ts`), not a permission error.
- Writes that target the project or anything in it (creating, updating, changing the status of, moving, assigning or archiving its issues; posting, editing or deleting comments on them; updating, archiving or restoring the project) also throw `NotFoundError` and change nothing.
- Listings, meaning the project list and the org-wide issue list, silently leave the project and its issues out, and their `total` counts only what the actor can see.
Changes to project membership or to the lead take effect immediately.

Export `canViewProject(actor: Actor, project: Project): Promise<boolean>` from `src/server/services/project-service.ts`, returning whether the actor may see the project under this rule. Search is out of scope for this change.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly.     name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	/**
2	 * Issue rows: the widest query surface in the app. Every method takes `orgId` first and honours `IssueFilter.includeArchived`.
3	 *
4	 * Must call (do not reimplement): archivePatch, restorePatch, shouldFilterArchived
5	 */
6	import {

8	  count,
9	  desc,
10	  eq,

55	/** Statuses whose entry stamps `completed_at`; leaving one clears it again. */

58	export async function findIssueById(
59	  orgId: OrgId,
60	  issueId: IssueId,
61	): Promise<Issue | null> {
62	  const row = getDb()
63	    .select()
64	    .from(issues)
65	    .where(and(orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId), eq(issues.id, issueId)))
66	    .get();
67	  if (!row) return null;
68	
69	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(orgId, [row.id as IssueId]);
70	  return toIssue(row, (labels[row.id] ?? []).map((label) => label.id));
71	}

74	  orgId: OrgId,

76	  issueNumber: number,

79	    .select()

84	        eq(issues.projectId, projectId),

92	/** Builds the shared predicate list behind `listIssues` and its count. */
93	function issueFilters(input: IssueFilterInput): readonly SQL[] {
94	  const scope: ArchiveScope = shouldFilterArchived(input)
95	    ? {}
96	    : { includeArchived: true };
97	
98	  return compact(
99	    orgPredicate(issues.orgId, input.orgId),
100	    livePredicate(issues.archivedAt, scope),
101	    input.projectId === undefined
102	      ? undefined
103	      : eq(issues.projectId, input.projectId),
104	    input.status === undefined || input.status.length === 0
105	      ? undefined
106	      : inArray(issues.status, [...input.status]),
107	    input.priority === undefined || input.priority.length === 0
108	      ? undefined
109	      : inArray(issues.priority, [...input.priority]),
110	    input.assigneeId === undefined
111	      ? undefined
112	      : input.assigneeId === null
113	        ? isNull(issues.assigneeId)
114	        : eq(issues.assigneeId, input.assigneeId),
115	    input.authorId === undefined
116	      ? undefined
117	      : eq(issues.authorId, input.authorId),
118	    input.dueBefore === undefined ? undefined : lt(issues.dueAt, input.dueBefore),
119	    input.query === undefined
120	      ? undefined
121	      : or(
122	          like(issues.title, `%${input.query}%`),
123	          like(issues.description, `%${input.query}%`),
124	        ),
125	    input.labelIds === undefined || input.labelIds.length === 0
126	      ? undefined
127	      : inArray(
128	          issues.id,
129	          getDb()
130	            .select({ id: issueLabels.issueId })
131	            .from(issueLabels)
132	            .where(
133	              and(
134	                orgPredicate(issueLabels.orgId, input.orgId),
135	                inArray(issueLabels.labelId, [...input.labelIds]),
136	              ),
137	            ),
138	        ),
139	  );
140	}

142	export async function listIssues(
143	  input: IssueFilterInput,
144	): Promise<Page<Issue>> {
145	  const db = getDb();
146	  const filters = issueFilters(input);
147	  const sort = { sortColumn: issues.createdAt, idColumn: issues.id };
148	
149	  const total = db
150	    .select({ value: count() })
151	    .from(issues)
152	    .where(and(...filters))
153	    .get();
154	
155	  const rows = db
156	    .select()
157	    .from(issues)
158	    .where(and(...filters, ...compact(keysetPredicate(sort, input.cursor))))
159	    .orderBy(desc(issues.createdAt), desc(issues.id))
160	    .limit(probeLimit(input.limit))
161	    .all();
162	
163	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(
164	    input.orgId,
165	    rows.map((row) => row.id as IssueId),
166	  );
167	
168	  return toPage(
169	    rows,
170	    input.limit,
171	    total?.value ?? 0,
172	    (row) => toIssue(row, (labels[row.id] ?? []).map((label) => label.id)),
173	    (row) => ({ id: row.id, sortValue: row.createdAt }),
174	  );
175	}

177	/**
178	 * The list view needs comment and attachment counts per row. Two grouped
179	 * queries beat N+1 round trips, so the counts are folded in afterwards.
180	 */
181	export async function listIssuesWithRelations(
182	  input: IssueFilterInput,
183	): Promise<Page<IssueWithRelations>> {
184	  const db = getDb();
185	  const page = await listIssues(input);
186	  const ids = page.items.map((issue) => issue.id);
187	  if (ids.length === 0) {
188	    return { items: [], nextCursor: page.nextCursor, total: page.total };
189	  }
190	
191	  const commentCounts = db
192	    .select({ issueId: comments.issueId, value: count() })
193	    .from(comments)
194	    .where(
195	      and(
196	        orgPredicate(comments.orgId, input.orgId),
197	        inArray(comments.issueId, [...ids]),
198	        isNull(comments.archivedAt),
199	      ),
200	    )
201	    .groupBy(comments.issueId)
202	    .all();
203	
204	  const attachmentCounts = db
205	    .select({ issueId: attachments.issueId, value: count() })
206	    .from(attachments)
207	    .where(
208	      and(
209	        orgPredicate(attachments.orgId, input.orgId),
210	        inArray(attachments.issueId, [...ids]),
211	      ),
212	    )
213	    .groupBy(attachments.issueId)
214	    .all();
215	
216	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(input.orgId, ids);
217	  const commentsBy = new Map(commentCounts.map((r) => [r.issueId, r.value]));
218	  const attachmentsBy = new Map(
219	    attachmentCounts.map((r) => [r.issueId, r.value]),
220	  );
221	
222	  return {
223	    items: page.items.map((issue) => ({
224	      issue,
225	      labels: labels[issue.id] ?? [],
226	      commentCount: commentsBy.get(issue.id) ?? 0,
227	      attachmentCount: attachmentsBy.get(issue.id) ?? 0,
228	    })),
229	    nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
230	    total: page.total,
231	  };
232	}

234	/** One column per status, in `ISSUE_STATUSES` order, live rows only. */
235	export async function listBoardColumns(
236	  orgId: OrgId,
237	  projectId: ProjectId,
238	): Promise<readonly IssueBoardColumn[]> {
239	  const rows = getDb()
240	    .select()
241	    .from(issues)
242	    .where(
243	      and(
244	        ...compact(
245	          orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId),
246	          eq(issues.projectId, projectId),
247	          livePredicate(issues.archivedAt, {}),
248	        ),
249	      ),
250	    )
251	    .orderBy(desc(issues.updatedAt))
252	    .all();
253	
254	  const labels = await listLabelsForIssues(

405	export async function setIssueStatus(
406	  orgId: OrgId,
407	  issueId: IssueId,
408	  status: IssueStatus,
409	): Promise<Issue> {
410	  const stamp = toIsoTimestamp(new Date());
411	  const current = getDb()
412	    .select()
413	    .from(issues)
414	    .where(and(orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId), eq(issues.id, issueId)))
415	    .get();
416	
417	  if (!current) throw new Error(`Issue ${issueId} not found`);
418	
419	  const row = getDb()
420	    .update(issues)
421	    .set({
422	      status,
423	      startedAt:
424	        status === "in_progress" && current.startedAt === null
425	          ? stamp
426	          : current.startedAt,
427	      completedAt: TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(status) ? stamp : null,
428	      updatedAt: stamp,
429	    })
430	    .where(and(orgPredicate(issues.orgId, orgId), eq(issues.id, issueId)))
431	    .returning()
432	    .get();
433	
434	  return toIssue(row);
